script_domains.description: Coinhive, the in-browser Monero miner that started the drive-by mining wave. The service shut down in 2019, so any surviving reference means stale injected code is still on the machine.
Coinhive's 'opt-in' branded endpoint, used to evade blocklists.
CoinIMP browser miner, a common Coinhive successor.
CryptoNight WebAssembly mining module, the hashing core of most browser miners.
deepMiner, a self-hosted open-source browser mining kit used after Coinhive shut down.

script_markers.description: CoinIMP/deepMiner client initialisation used by several browser mining kits.
CryptoNight hashing algorithm reference inside browser code.
Stratum mining protocol URL embedded in browser or extension code.
Mining start call used by several browser mining libraries.

extensions.name: SafeBrowse
extensions.description: Chrome extension that was caught running a hidden Monero miner in the background of every browsing session.

extensions.name: Archive Poster
extensions.description: Tumblr helper extension that was compromised and shipped a hidden Coinhive miner to its users.

extensions.name: Ldoco
extensions.description: Extension family repeatedly re-uploaded to the Chrome Web Store carrying browser mining payloads.

extensions.description: Extension advertising in-browser mining. Only expected if the device owner deliberately installed it.
